children: Solar Industries India Ltd shares gained 1.5 percent in early trade on Tuesday after Jefferies initiated coverage on the defence and explosives manufacturer with a 'buy' rating, citing strong growth prospects for India's private-sector defence companies.

Solar Industries shares were trading at Rs 22,280 in early trade, up 1.5 percent from the previous close of Rs 21,950. The stock has surged around 83 percent so far in 2026, sharply outperforming the Nifty 50, which is down around 9 percent over the same period. The company's market capitalisation stands at around Rs 2 lakh crore.
Jefferies initiated coverage on Solar Industries with a target price of Rs 28,160 per share, implying around 28 percent upside from Monday's closing price.

The brokerage expects Indian defence spending to grow at a double-digit compound annual growth rate over the medium term, with the government's emphasis on domestic manufacturing providing a particularly strong opportunity for private-sector companies. Jefferies expects private defence companies to potentially deliver growth of more than 20 percent.

The bullish view comes as the government steps up defence procurement and pushes a greater share of orders towards domestic manufacturers.

The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, on Monday accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) to acquisition proposals worth around Rs 1.10 lakh crore across the Army, Navy and Air Force. Around 98 percent of the proposed procurement has been earmarked for Indian industry.
The approvals cover a range of equipment, including Advanced Light Helicopters, high-mobility vehicles, mechanical mine layers, radars, marine gas turbines and ground-based multi-purpose jammers.

Motilal Oswal Financial Services said defence acquisition approvals in FY27 so far have reached Rs 1.62 lakh crore, while approvals from FY25 through FY27 year-to-date total around Rs 13 lakh crore, expanding the addressable market for domestic defence manufacturers.

The brokerage also highlighted the government's move towards opening missile production to private-sector companies, which could further widen the opportunity for non-PSU defence manufacturers. It said these initiatives improve order-inflow visibility for the domestic defence industry.

title: Solar Industries shares rise 1.5%; Jefferies bullish on private defence growth with indigenisation push
